doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Joe Williams tries to jump on the piano
summary: Williams tried repeatedly to climb the piano to sing a torch song, and the band collapsed laughing.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I can’t recall, and if I could, I’m sure I wouldn’t want to repeat them. There were so many incidents, so many amusing incidents. It would be a whole other interview to tell all the incidents, but I’ll tell this one other one. Joe Williams, he loved to sing ballads and torch songs. He not only sang the blues. So he was singing. I forget what the name -- what club it was. It might have been the Blue Note in Chicago. He was all tuxed out, clean. He was singing this song, and he wanted to get a little extra torchy. You know how in the old days the torch singers used to jump up on the piano, the top of the piano? They’d jump on the piano to sing their blues song.
I thought mostly ladies did that.

Mostly ladies did, and it should have stayed that way. Joe walked over to the piano with the microphone in hand. He was singing, and he was trying to get up [laughs]. He tried about three or four times, still singing [laughs], and he never made it. Needless to say, the band, we just fell apart [laughs]. Describing this scene is nothing like seeing it. If you could have seen some 200-plus-pounds of Joe Williams trying to jump up on this piano to get torchy, you would --
He wasn’t Jimmy Rushing, but he was still big.
Yeah. He was tall and muscular, yeah. They were just too numerous to mention.
